reasons: Overlaps on machine learning, robotics, reinforcement learning
subject: Interested in your robot learning work
body:
Hello Professor Finn,

My name is Vinil Polepalli and I am an undergraduate at New York University studying Computer Science and Business. I was a machine learning research intern at the Carnegie Mellon Robotics Institute, where I trained a PyTorch semantic segmentation model to 0.88 mean IoU and 0.94 F1 on 25,000 labeled aerial images and put it into an autonomous UAV pipeline running under 100 ms per frame.

I read MAML, and what I find most useful is that it asks nothing of the architecture: optimizing for parameters a few gradient steps away from good on any task in the distribution covers classification, regression and policy learning alike. The cost that made this concrete for me was those 25,000 labels, which came from one project's flights, so a new species or site means labeling again. I would want to treat each species-site pair as a task and measure how few labeled tiles a MAML-initialized model needs to match what we got from the full set.

I would like to hear more about what the lab is working on now, and where my background would be useful to you.

In the past, I have worked on the following related projects:
- Sole author, cVAE-augmented deep learning for pan-cancer RNA-seq classification, about 98% test accuracy across 5 cancer types on TCGA: https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.02743
- Hsp90 inhibitor virtual screening in the Chiosis Lab at Memorial Sloan Kettering: 4,566 candidates screened at 0.984 GNN ROC AUC and 5x enrichment, 0 Lipinski violations in the top 50: https://hsp90-dashboard.vercel.app/
- First author, EGCG and piperine synergy in D. tigrina regeneration, IEEE MIT Undergraduate Research Technology Conference: https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/11533121

Outside of research I was invited to Y Combinator's Startup School, reached the VEX Robotics World Championship semifinals, and have qualified for the AIME three times.

I have extensively used PyTorch, OpenCV and Python in past work, but have a lot of coding experience and am adaptable to whichever libraries your lab uses. My resume is attached. Please let me know if there is a fit in your lab.

I would be happy to elaborate on my skills and where I think I can best help out.

Thank you!

--
Vinil Polepalli
New York University | Class of 2029
B.S. Computer Science and B.S. Business
